chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated on the authority of 'Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad and others, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sulayman, on the authority of 'Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, that Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) said:

He said: Verily, Allah is the Most Great, and the Lofty. Worshippers cannot describe Him, nor can they reach the core of His Magnificence. Vision comprehends Him not, and He comprehends (all) vision; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware. He cannot be described in terms of 'how,' 'where,' and 'when.' And how can I describe Him by means of 'how' when it is He who created the condition for the question 'how'; hence, I recognized the condition by the fact that He created the 'how.' And how can I describe Him in terms of 'where' when it was He who created space; hence, I recognized space by the fact that He created the 'where.' And how can I describe Him in terms of 'when' when it was He who created time; hence, I recognized time by the fact that He created time. Thus, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is present in every place, and is absent from everything. Vision comprehends Him not, and He comprehends all vision. There is no god but He: the Most High, the Great. And He is the Knower of subtleties, the Aware.
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about describing Allah's attributes and His relationship to space and time?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih) by arguing that since Allah created the categories of 'how' (kayf), 'where' (ayn), and 'place' (hayth), He cannot be confined by them. It concludes with the nuanced view that God is 'inside' all places yet 'outside' all things, a concept central to understanding how the Unseen can be perceived without being limited by spatial dimensions. This passage is frequently cited in Shia kalām to refute anthropomorphism while affirming God's omnipresence.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 14. Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isam al-Kulayni (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Ya`qub al-Kulayni said on the authority of `Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad and others, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sulayman, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja`fari, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan, that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Verily, Allah is the Most Great, and the Lofty [al-rafi`]. Worshippers cannot describe Him, nor can they reach the core of His Magnificence. Vision comprehends Him not, and He comprehends (all) vision; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware. He cannot be described in terms of `how,’ `where’ and `when’. And how can I describe him by means of `how’ when it is He who created the condition for the question `how;’ hence, I recognized the condition by the fact that He created the `how.’ And how can I describe Him in terms of `where’ when it was He was created space; hence, I recognized space by the fact that he created the `where.’ And how can I describe him in terms of `when’ when it was he who created time; hence, I recognized time by the fact that He created time. Thus, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is present in every place, and is absent from everything. Vision comprehends Him not, and He comprehends all vision. There is no god but He: the Most High, the Great. And He is the Knower of subtleties, the Aware.
